--- title: "Selectors & Expression Expansion" subtitle: "≈ tidyselect · `across()` · `if_any()` / `if_all()` · `c_across()`" jupyter: python3 --- dplyr uses three extra mechanisms for many columns: tidyselect picks them, `across()` maps functions over them, and `if_any()` / `if_all()` / `c_across()` work across a row. Polars has one: an expression whose root names **several columns** is rewritten into one expression per column before it runs. This chapter covers that rewrite, the `polars.selectors` algebra, the `across()` patterns built on it, the `*_horizontal` row-wise functions, and the places where a selector silently turns into arithmetic. ## In tidyverse {#sec-sel-tidyverse} ```r library(dplyr) library(palmerpenguins) penguins |> summarise( across(where(is.numeric) & !year, list(mean = \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), sd = \(x) sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)), .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"), .by = species ) penguins |> filter(if_any(ends_with("_mm"), \(x) x > 50)) penguins |> rowwise() |> mutate(mm_med = median(c_across(ends_with("_mm")))) |> ungroup() ``` tidyselect evaluates its helpers against the data frame, and `across()` loops over the result, naming outputs with glue. Polars replaces the selection with an object you can hold, and the loop with a rewrite. ## Mental model {#sec-sel-model} ```text YOU WRITE ONE EXPRESSION EXPANSION (needs only the schema) CONTEXT RUNS N EXPRESSIONS ───────────────────────── ───────────────────────────────────────── ────────────────────────── cs.ends_with("_mm") col("bill_length_mm").mean() bill_length_mm_mean .mean() ──────► .alias("bill_length_mm_mean") ──────► bill_depth_mm_mean .name.suffix("_mean") col("bill_depth_mm").mean() … flipper_length_mm_mean col("flipper_length_mm").mean() … ``` The root of the expression (`pl.col(...)`, a `cs.*` selector, `pl.all()`) is matched against column **names and dtypes**, never values. Every method chained after it is copied onto each match, and the context sees N ordinary expressions, as if you had typed them. So `across()` is not a function in Polars: it is what happens to any expression whose root matches more than one column. In Polars 2.0, every multi-column root is a selector under the hood: | You write | Internally | Expansion order | |---|---|---| | `pl.col("a")` | a single column | — | | `pl.col("a", "b")`, `pl.col(["a", "b"])` | `cs.by_name("a", "b")` | as listed | | `pl.col("^bill_.*$")` | `cs.matches("^bill_.*$")` | frame order | | `pl.col(pl.Float64)` | `cs.by_dtype([Float64])` | frame order | | `pl.all()` / `pl.exclude("a")` | `cs.all()` / `cs.all() - cs.by_name("a", require_all=False)` | frame order | | `pl.nth(0, -1)` / `pl.first()` | `cs.by_index(0, -1)` / `cs.first()` | as listed | | `cs.numeric()`, `cs.starts_with(...)` … | a `Selector` object | frame order | : The roots that expand {.striped} ## Mechanics {#sec-sel-mechanics} ::: {#1c3e3b29 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import datetime as dt from decimal import Decimal import polars as pl import polars.selectors as cs from pl_notes import datasets penguins_df = datasets.penguins() flights_df = datasets.flights() ``` ::: ### One expression, many outputs {#sec-sel-expansion} ::: {#f555534f .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} bill_means = pl.col("bill_length_mm", "bill_depth_mm").mean() print(bill_means) penguins_df.select(bill_means) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` cs.by_name('bill_length_mm', 'bill_depth_mm', require_all=true).mean() ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
shape: (1, 2)
bill_length_mmbill_depth_mm

43.9219317.15117
``` ::: ::: It prints as a selector, `.meta.has_multiple_outputs()` is `True`, and `.meta.output_name()` raises: there is no single name. In a context it becomes two columns, each named after its own input. The lazy plan shows the rewrite: three ordinary expressions, the suffix turned into an `alias`: ::: {#459df4a6 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} print(penguins_df.lazy().select(cs.ends_with("_mm").mean().name.suffix("_mean")).explain()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` SELECT [col("bill_length_mm").mean().alias("bill_length_mm_mean"), col("bill_depth_mm").mean().alias("bill_depth_mm_mean"), col("flipper_length_mm").mean().alias("flipper_length_mm_mean")] DF ["species", "island", "bill_length_mm", "bill_depth_mm", ...]; PROJECT["bill_length_mm", "bill_depth_mm", "flipper_length_mm"] 3/8 COLUMNS ``` ::: ::: When a multi-output expression meets another operand, the output counts on each side decide: ```text many ⊕ one [a, b] / c → a / c, b / c the single side is reused many ⊕ many (same) [a, b] / [c, d] → a / c, b / d zipped by position, not crossed many ⊕ many (≠) [a, b] / [c, d, e] → error ``` ::: {#7a6702c6 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} penguins_df.head(2).select( pl.col("bill_length_mm", "bill_depth_mm") / pl.col("flipper_length_mm", "body_mass_g") ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: 39.1 / 181 = 0.216 and 18.7 / 3750 = 0.005: zipped, and named after the left side. Different counts raise: ::: {#25859aae .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} penguins_df.select(cs.ends_with("_mm") / pl.col("body_mass_g", "year")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html} 
InvalidOperationError: cannot combine selectors that produce a different number of columns (2 != 3)
``` ::: ::: ::: ### `pl.col()`: names, patterns, dtypes {#sec-sel-col} A string is a **pattern** only if it starts with `^` and ends with `$`: ::: {#a00066af .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} ( penguins_df.select(pl.col("year", "species")).columns, penguins_df.select(pl.col("^bill_.*$")).columns, penguins_df.select(pl.col(pl.Int64, pl.Float64)).columns, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ``` (['year', 'species'], ['bill_length_mm', 'bill_depth_mm'], ['bill_length_mm', 'bill_depth_mm', 'flipper_length_mm', 'body_mass_g', 'year']) ``` ::: ::: Names keep the order you list and raise `ColumnNotFoundError` if missing. Patterns (Rust regex syntax) and dtypes keep frame order, and a pattern that matches nothing returns zero columns without an error. A dtype class (`pl.Datetime`) matches every parameterization; an instance (`pl.Datetime("us")`) matches exactly (@sec-sel-dtype-trap). Older dtype groups such as `pl.NUMERIC_DTYPES` don't exist in 2.0: use `cs.numeric()`. ### The `polars.selectors` catalogue {#sec-sel-cs} One-line translations are in the cheatsheet ([Select Columns](../overview/polars-cheatsheet.qmd#sec-cs-select)). The full set, grouped by what each selector looks at: | Looks at | Polars | tidyselect | |---|---|---| | dtype | `cs.numeric()`, `cs.integer()`, `cs.signed_integer()`, `cs.unsigned_integer()`, `cs.float()`, `cs.decimal()` | `where(is.numeric)`, `where(is.integer)`, `where(is.double)` | | | `cs.string()`, `cs.categorical()`, `cs.enum()`, `cs.boolean()`, `cs.binary()` | `where(is.character)`, `where(is.factor)`, `where(is.logical)` | | | `cs.temporal()`, `cs.date()`, `cs.datetime(time_unit, time_zone)`, `cs.duration()`, `cs.time()` | `where(is.Date)`, `where(is.POSIXct)` (lubridate) | | | `cs.nested()`, `cs.list()`, `cs.array()`, `cs.struct()`, `cs.by_dtype(...)` | `where(is.list)`, `where(is.data.frame)` | | name | `cs.by_name(..., require_all=True)` | `all_of()`; `require_all=False` ≈ `any_of()` | | | `cs.starts_with()`, `cs.ends_with()`, `cs.contains()`: literal; several args = OR | `starts_with()`, `ends_with()`, `contains()` | | | `cs.matches(regex)`: unanchored, unlike `pl.col()` | `matches()` | | position | `cs.by_index(0, -1)`, `cs.by_index(range(2, 6))`, `cs.first()`, `cs.last()` | `c(1, last_col())`, `3:6` | | everything | `cs.all()`, `cs.exclude(...)`, `cs.empty()` | `everything()`, `-c(...)` | : Selector catalogue (positions are 0-based) {.striped} There is no name range like `bill_length_mm:body_mass_g` (use `cs.by_index(range(...))`), and no `where(fn)` that inspects values: selectors see only the schema (@sec-sel-recipes has the workaround). Group membership is not always what an R user expects. A frame with one column per dtype: ::: {#f0579a58 .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} dtype_zoo_df = pl.DataFrame( { "i64": [1], "u32": [1], "f64": [1.0], "dec": [Decimal("1.5")], "bool": [True], "str": ["a"], "cat": ["a"], "enum": ["a"], "date": [dt.date(2025, 1, 1)], "dtm": [dt.datetime(2025, 1, 1)], "dtm_utc": [dt.datetime(2025, 1, 1, tzinfo=dt.UTC)], "dur": [dt.timedelta(days=1)], "time": [dt.time(9)], "list": [[1]], "struct": [{"a": 1}], }, schema_overrides={"u32": pl.UInt32, "cat": pl.Categorical, "enum": pl.Enum(["a"])}, ) { name: cs.expand_selector(dtype_zoo_df, getattr(cs, name)()) for name in ["numeric", "integer", "categorical", "temporal", "datetime", "nested"] } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ``` {'numeric': ('i64', 'u32', 'f64', 'dec'), 'integer': ('i64', 'u32'), 'categorical': ('cat',), 'temporal': ('date', 'dtm', 'dtm_utc', 'dur', 'time'), 'datetime': ('dtm', 'dtm_utc'), 'nested': ('list', 'struct')} ``` ::: ::: `Decimal` is numeric and `Boolean` is not (in R, `is.numeric(TRUE)` is `FALSE` too). `Enum` is not `categorical`: use `cs.enum()`. `temporal` includes `Duration` and `Time`. `cs.datetime()` matches naive and tz-aware columns; narrow it with `time_zone=None` or `time_zone="*"` (any zone). **Previewing.** `cs.expand_selector()` resolves a selector against a `DataFrame`, a `LazyFrame` or a schema and returns the names, computing nothing; `strict=False` also accepts `pl.col()` / `pl.all()` roots: ::: {#9e423893 .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} ( cs.expand_selector(flights_df.lazy(), cs.integer() - cs.by_name("year", "month", "day")), cs.expand_selector(penguins_df.schema, pl.col("^bill_.*$"), strict=False), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=9} ``` (('dep_time', 'sched_dep_time', 'dep_delay', 'arr_time', 'sched_arr_time', 'arr_delay', 'flight', 'air_time', 'distance', 'hour', 'minute'), ('bill_length_mm', 'bill_depth_mm')) ``` ::: ::: ### Set algebra {#sec-sel-algebra} | Polars | Meaning | tidyselect | |---|---|---| | `a | b` | union | `a | b`, `c(a, b)` | | `a & b` | intersection | `a & b` | | `a - b` | difference | `a & !b` | | `a ^ b` | in exactly one | — | | `~a` | complement (`cs.all() - a`) | `!a` | : Selector set operators {.striped} ::: {#0c2e41e5 .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} ( cs.expand_selector(flights_df, cs.ends_with("_time") - cs.starts_with("sched")), cs.expand_selector(penguins_df, cs.by_name("year", "species")), cs.expand_selector(penguins_df, cs.by_name("year") | cs.by_name("species")), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=10} ``` (('dep_time', 'arr_time', 'air_time'), ('year', 'species'), ('species', 'year')) ``` ::: ::: **Order rule.** A single `by_name()` / `by_index()` keeps the order you wrote; any set operation returns **frame order**. So does `pl.col("year", "^bill_.*$")`, because a pattern among the names makes it a union. For a chosen order, pass separate arguments: `select("year", cs.all() - cs.by_name("year"))`. ### Selector or expression? {#sec-sel-dispatch} `Selector` subclasses `Expr`, so `-`, `&`, `|`, `^` and `~` each mean two things. Python decides from the operand types: | Expression | Result | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `selector - selector` (also `&`, `|`, `^`), `~selector` | `Selector` | set operation | | `selector + selector`, `*`, `/`, `>`, `==` …; `selector - pl.col("x")`, `- "x"`, `- 1` | `Expr` | arithmetic / comparison | | `selector | pl.col("x")` | `Expr` | **bitwise** or (logical on Booleans) | | `pl.col("x") - selector`, `1 - selector` | `TypeError` | use `selector.as_expr()` | | `selector.mean()`, `selector.name.suffix(...)`, any method | `Expr` | no more set algebra | : Operator dispatch, verified on Polars 2.0 {.striped} ::: {#8521b110 .cell execution_count=11} ``` {.python .cell-code} penguins_df.select(1 - cs.float()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html} 
TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for op: ('Expr' - 'Selector')
``` ::: ::: ::: `.as_expr()` turns a selector into a plain expression (`expr.meta.as_selector()` goes back). `.name.keep()` is needed below because `1 - x` is named `literal`, its leftmost input: ::: {#4011a679 .cell execution_count=12} ``` {.python .cell-code} penguins_df.head(2).select((1 - cs.float().as_expr()).name.keep()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=12} ```{=html}

Pass it the selector and everything inside expands: ::: {#be7576d9 .cell execution_count=13} ``` {.python .cell-code} def scale(e: pl.Expr) -> pl.Expr: """as.numeric(scale(x)): centre, then divide by the SD.""" return (e - e.mean()) / e.std() penguins_df.select(scale(cs.ends_with("_mm"))).head(2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=13} ```{=html}

If order matters, loop over the names yourself: ::: {#4a2e5037 .cell execution_count=15} ``` {.python .cell-code} fns = {"mean": pl.Expr.mean, "sd": pl.Expr.std} # ≈ list(mean = mean, sd = sd) mm_cols = cs.expand_selector(penguins_df, cs.ends_with("_mm")) penguins_df.select( fn(pl.col(c)).alias(f"{c}_{fn_name}") for c in mm_cols for fn_name, fn in fns.items() ).columns ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=15} ``` ['bill_length_mm_mean', 'bill_length_mm_sd', 'bill_depth_mm_mean', 'bill_depth_mm_sd', 'flipper_length_mm_mean', 'flipper_length_mm_sd'] ``` ::: ::: | `across(.names = )` | Polars, chained after the computation | |---|---| | `"{.col}"` (default, one function) | nothing: each output keeps its input's name | | `"{.col}_{.fn}"` / `"{.fn}_{.col}"` | `.name.suffix("_mean")` / `.name.prefix("mean_")` | | `"{toupper(.col)}"` | `.name.to_uppercase()`, `.name.to_lowercase()` | | `"{str_remove(.col, '_mm')}"` | `.name.replace("_mm$", "")` (regex; `literal=True`), `.name.strip_suffix("_mm")` | | any function of the name | `.name.map(lambda c: ...)` | | (back to the root column's name) | `.name.keep()` | : `.names` glue specs → the `.name` namespace {.striped} `.name.suffix()`, `.prefix()` and `.map()` act on the **current** output name: after `.alias("z")` they give `z_…`, although the docstring says "root column name". Only `.name.keep()` returns to the root. **Selectors skip the group keys.** Inside `group_by().agg()`, a selector or `pl.all()` leaves out the grouping columns, like `across()` in a grouped `summarise()`. `year` is numeric but not aggregated: ::: {#3e4be060 .cell execution_count=16} ``` {.python .cell-code} penguins_df.group_by("year").agg(cs.numeric().mean()).sort("year") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=16} ```{=html}

Row-wise work goes **across** columns, through `pl.*` functions that take many expressions (a selector counts as many) and return one value per row: | tidyverse | Polars | |---|---| | `rowSums(pick(...), na.rm = TRUE)` / `rowMeans(...)` | `pl.sum_horizontal(...)` / `pl.mean_horizontal(...)` | | `pmin()` / `pmax()` | `pl.min_horizontal()` / `pl.max_horizontal()` | | `if_all(cols, fn)` / `if_any(cols, fn)` | `pl.all_horizontal(fn(sel))` / `pl.any_horizontal(fn(sel))` | | `str_c(a, b, sep = "-")` / `unite()` | `pl.concat_str(a, b, separator="-")` | | `rowwise()` + `f(c_across(cols))` | `pl.concat_list(sel).list.f()` | | `pick(a, b)` as one value per row | `pl.struct(a, b)` | : Row-wise equivalents {.striped} ::: {#b6d8eb1f .cell execution_count=17} ``` {.python .cell-code} nulls_df = pl.DataFrame({"a": [1, None, None], "b": [10, 20, None]}) nulls_df.with_columns( sum=pl.sum_horizontal("a", "b"), sum_strict=pl.sum_horizontal("a", "b", ignore_nulls=False), mean=pl.mean_horizontal("a", "b"), max=pl.max_horizontal("a", "b"), plus=pl.col("a") + pl.col("b"), str=pl.concat_str("a", "b", separator="-"), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=17} ```{=html}

An all-null row sums to **0** (as `rowSums(na.rm = TRUE)` does); its mean is null (R: `NaN`). - `+` and `concat_str()` propagate nulls, like `str_c()`; `concat_str(..., ignore_nulls=True)` skips them, like `unite(na.rm = TRUE)`. - `all_horizontal()` / `any_horizontal()` use the three-valued logic of `&` / `|`: `any(null, true)` is `true`, `any(null, false)` is null. **`if_any()` / `if_all()`.** A multi-output predicate in `filter()` is refused, not silently combined: ::: {#e101fb0a .cell execution_count=18} ``` {.python .cell-code} flights_df.filter(cs.ends_with("_delay") > 60) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html} 
ComputeError: The predicate passed to 'LazyFrame.filter' expanded to multiple expressions: 

	[(col("dep_delay")) > (dyn int: 60)],
	[(col("arr_delay")) > (dyn int: 60)],
This is ambiguous. Try to combine the predicates with the 'all_horizontal' or `any_horizontal' expression.
``` ::: ::: ::: Say which reduction you mean. The comparison is a value, so keep it in a variable: ::: {#6eac424b .cell execution_count=19} ``` {.python .cell-code} very_late = cs.ends_with("_delay") > 60 # dep_delay, arr_delay flights_df.select( any_late=pl.any_horizontal(very_late), all_late=pl.all_horizontal(very_late), ).select(pl.all().sum(), pl.all().null_count().name.suffix("_null")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=19} ```{=html}

Mixed `Int64` / `Float64` inputs are cast to their supertype: ::: {#f2ff64de .cell execution_count=20} ``` {.python .cell-code} mm_row = pl.concat_list(cs.ends_with("_mm")) penguins_df.slice(2, 3).select( cs.ends_with("_mm"), mm_median=mm_row.list.median(), mm_n=mm_row.list.drop_nulls().list.len(), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=20} ```{=html}

-1967.5-1989.6-182117930
``` ::: ::: The intent was "numeric except `year`". The result subtracts 2007 from every numeric column (`year - year = 0`), with no warning. `cs.integer() | pl.col("year")` is worse: a bitwise OR of integers. **Rule:** set operations need a selector on **both** sides: `cs.numeric() - cs.by_name("year")` (raises on a typo) or `cs.numeric().exclude("year")` (ignores one). ### Names after expansion {#sec-sel-name-trap} `.alias()` gives every expanded expression the same name: ::: {#ceccb20c .cell execution_count=23} ``` {.python .cell-code} penguins_df.select(cs.ends_with("_mm").mean().alias("mm_mean")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html} 
DuplicateError: projections contained duplicate output name 'mm_mean'. It's possible that multiple expressions are returning the same default column name. If this is the case, try renaming the columns with `.alias("new_name")` to avoid duplicate column names.
``` ::: ::: ::: The same code works whenever the selector happens to match one column, so it breaks only when the data changes. Use `.name.suffix()` / `.name.map()`. With the selector on the right, every output takes the left operand's name: ::: {#5d4484d5 .cell execution_count=24} ``` {.python .cell-code} penguins_df.select(pl.col("body_mass_g") / cs.ends_with("_mm")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html} 
DuplicateError: projections contained duplicate output name 'body_mass_g'. It's possible that multiple expressions are returning the same default column name. If this is the case, try renaming the columns with `.alias("new_name")` to avoid duplicate column names.
``` ::: ::: ::: `.name.keep()` doesn't help (the root is still `body_mass_g`): put the selector on the left, or loop over `cs.expand_selector()` with `.alias()`. The `*_horizontal` functions follow the same rule, which in `with_columns()` means a silent overwrite: here `bill_length_mm` is replaced by the sum. ::: {#77ac33f6 .cell execution_count=25} ``` {.python .cell-code} penguins_df.head(2).with_columns( pl.sum_horizontal("bill_length_mm", "bill_depth_mm") ).select(cs.starts_with("bill")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=25} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Always name a horizontal result: `bill_total=pl.sum_horizontal(...)`. ### Patterns that aren't patterns {#sec-sel-regex-trap} ::: {#b11a0289 .cell execution_count=26} ``` {.python .cell-code} penguins_df.select(pl.col("^bill")) # no trailing $ → a literal column name ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html} 
ColumnNotFoundError: unable to find column "^bill"; valid columns: ["species", "island", "bill_length_mm", "bill_depth_mm", "flipper_length_mm", "body_mass_g", "sex", "year"]
``` ::: ::: ::: `pl.exclude()` is `by_name(require_all=False)` underneath, so the same mistake, or a typo, excludes nothing and raises nothing: ::: {#f3ed5424 .cell execution_count=27} ``` {.python .cell-code} penguins_df.select(pl.exclude("^bill", "yaer")).columns ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=27} ``` ['species', 'island', 'bill_length_mm', 'bill_depth_mm', 'flipper_length_mm', 'body_mass_g', 'sex', 'year'] ``` ::: ::: `df.drop("yaer")` and `cs.all() - cs.by_name("yaer")` do raise. Literal selectors overmatch too: on `flights`, `cs.contains("time")` also picks up `time_hour`; `cs.ends_with("_time")` does not. ### Dtype instances match exactly {#sec-sel-dtype-trap} `flights.time_hour` is `Datetime("us", "America/New_York")`: ::: {#f9fc2ccd .cell execution_count=28} ``` {.python .cell-code} ( flights_df.select(pl.col(pl.Datetime("us"))).columns, # means time_zone=None flights_df.select(pl.col(pl.Datetime)).columns, # any unit, any zone cs.expand_selector(flights_df, cs.datetime("us")), # any zone by default ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=28} ``` ([], ['time_hour'], ('time_hour',)) ``` ::: ::: The first selects nothing, silently. Prefer the `cs.*` dtype selectors: they ignore the parameters you don't name. ## Recipes {#sec-sel-recipes} **Standardize every numeric column within groups** (≈ `mutate(across(where(is.numeric) & !year, \(x) as.numeric(scale(x)), .names = "{.col}_z"), .by = species)`): ::: {#a66087ce .cell execution_count=29} ``` {.python .cell-code} penguins_df.with_columns( scale(cs.numeric() - cs.by_name("year")).over("species").name.suffix("_z") ).select("species", cs.ends_with("_z")).head(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=29} ```{=html}

Build a mapping instead: ::: {#e464b0ff .cell execution_count=32} ``` {.python .cell-code} penguins_df.rename( {c: c.removesuffix("_mm") for c in cs.expand_selector(penguins_df, cs.ends_with("_mm"))} ).columns ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=32} ``` ['species', 'island', 'bill_length', 'bill_depth', 'flipper_length', 'body_mass_g', 'sex', 'year'] ``` ::: ::: ## See also {#sec-sel-see-also} - Cheatsheet: [Select Columns](../overview/polars-cheatsheet.qmd#sec-cs-select) · [Create & Modify Columns](../overview/polars-cheatsheet.qmd#sec-cs-mutate) (`across()`) · [Filter Rows](../overview/polars-cheatsheet.qmd#sec-cs-filter) (`if_any()` / `if_all()`) · [Programming with Polars](../overview/polars-cheatsheet.qmd#sec-cs-programming) - Related: [Expressions & Contexts](expressions.qmd) · [Data Model & Dtypes](data-model.qmd) · [Grouping & Aggregation](../transform/group-agg.qmd) · [Window Functions](../transform/window.qmd) · [Reshaping](../transform/reshape.qmd) (`unpivot()`) · [Missing Values](../types/missing.qmd) (null semantics) - Polars user guide: [Expression expansion](https://docs.pola.rs/user-guide/expressions/expression-expansion/) - Python API: [Selectors](https://docs.pola.rs/api/python/stable/reference/selectors.html) · [`Expr.name`](https://docs.pola.rs/api/python/stable/reference/expressions/name.html) - R: `?tidyselect::language`; dplyr `vignette("colwise")` and `vignette("rowwise")`
